body.statement:
Outside the now-solved subfamily \(d=1\), \(\beta=1\), and \(\alpha\geq1\), use \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{rob}}\) to determine \(\rho_{\mathrm{eval}}(n,\epsilon;d,\alpha,\beta,\kappa,L)\) and construct \(T_n^\star\) so that, jointly for all \(n\geq2\) and \(0\leq\epsilon\leq1/10\),
\[
c_0\rho_{\mathrm{eval}}
\leq\mathfrak R_n(\epsilon;d,\alpha,\beta,\kappa,L)
\leq\sup_{(P,Q,R)\in\mathcal C_{d,\alpha,\beta,\kappa,L}(\epsilon)}
\mathbb E_{R^n}|T_n^\star-\theta(P)|
\leq C_0\rho_{\mathrm{eval}}.
\]
The unresolved coordinates are \(d>1\), \(\beta\neq1\), or \(\alpha<1\), including their interactions and every logarithm on the remaining equality surfaces. The rate must be an explicit finite piecewise formula, the estimator must be total, finite, data-only, and computationally specified, and the converse must use the same contaminated experiment. The result must decide whether the clean functional rate and \(\omega_\theta(\epsilon/(1-\epsilon))\) are simultaneously attainable there or whether a quantified nuisance--contamination interaction is unavoidable.

obligation.what_is_open: For d greater than one, beta different from one, or alpha below one, construct a total finite data-only robust slabwise projected correction whose nuisance pilots and Gram matrices remain uniformly controlled above stable local occupancy, or prove a same-class interaction lower bound; then optimize every remaining balance, including equality-case logarithms.
obligation.obstruction: The all-kappa cell proof uses one-dimensional Lipschitz covariance bias and direct boundary reconstruction. Outside that subfamily, the frozen projection handle states no quantitative robustness inequality. A point or diffuse contaminant in one fine projected cell leaves an epsilon-squared kernel-diagonal term growing with projection dimension and inverse overlap; coordinatewise robustification does not control all pair terms below stable local occupancy, while occupancy truncation can erase the clean high-resolution gain. This is estimator-specific and therefore is not itself a minimax interaction converse.
obligation.attempted: The projected nuisance-product identity was expanded under point and diffuse within-cell contamination. Clean degeneracy removes first-order pilot bias, but the contaminated Hoeffding expectation retains the epsilon-squared diagonal. Range bounds force a projection resolution below that needed for the clean fast-functional correction, and anomaly filtering prevents this failure from serving as a universal lower-bound witness.
obligation.partial_result:
On the entire solved subfamily \(d=1\), \(\beta=1\), \(\alpha\geq1\), and \(\kappa>0\), \(\texttt{thm:lipschitz-all-kappa}\) proves simultaneous attainment:
\[
\mathfrak R_n(\epsilon;1,\alpha,1,\kappa,L)
\asymp_{\alpha,\kappa,L}
r_{n,\kappa}+\epsilon^{2/(\kappa+2)},
\]
with \(r_{n,\kappa}=n^{-1/2}\) for \(0<\kappa<1\), \(r_{n,1}=\{\log(en)/n\}^{1/2}\), and \(r_{n,\kappa}=n^{-2/(\kappa+3)}\) for \(\kappa>1\). For the remaining coordinates, the established same-experiment facts still imply
\[
\mathfrak R_n(\epsilon;d,\alpha,\beta,\kappa,L)
\geq\mathfrak R_n(0;d,\alpha,\beta,\kappa,L)
\quad\text{and}\quad
\mathfrak R_n(\epsilon;d,\alpha,\beta,\kappa,L)
\geq c\left(\frac{\epsilon}{1-\epsilon}\right)^{(\beta+1)/(\beta+\kappa+1)}.
\]
The first inequality follows by taking \(Q=P\). The second follows from the bump pair underlying \(\texttt{thm:ate-tv-modulus}\) and the explicit Jordan collision used in \(\texttt{lem:lipschitz-lower-pair-all-kappa}\). No general upper bound or matching interaction lower bound has been derived beyond the solved subfamily.

body.justification: The remaining first-class extension asks whether simultaneous attainment persists beyond one-dimensional Lipschitz outcomes and propensity calibration of smoothness at least one.
body.gap: Clean higher-order projection results and generic Huber testing do not control contaminated high-resolution pilots, empirical Gram matrices, and pair corrections on the remaining boundary classes.
body.consumer: Resolving the narrowed question would extend the practical error-radius benchmark to multidimensional and non-Lipschitz nuisance regimes.
